criteria: Appropriate diagnosis supported by documentation in the patient record.
Failed 30-day trials of two preferred antihypertensives within 6 months, OR allergy/contraindication to all preferred agents, OR documented stable therapy on the requested drug 60+ days.
Prior trials are judged within the same AHFS class (e.g. a non-preferred ACE inhibitor needs two preferred ACE inhibitors).

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the 'ACE Inhibitors' subsection (page 10 of the PDF) of Alabama Medicaid's PDL Reference Tool, effective 07/01/2026. Quinapril, enalapril, benazepril, and lisinopril (plus their HCTZ combinations and brand equivalents Accupril/Epaned/Lotensin/Zestril/Zestoretic/Accuretic/Lotensin HCT) are in the Preferred Generic column (no PA); captopril, fosinopril, moexipril, perindopril, ramipril, and trandolapril (plus combos) are in the Non-Preferred/PA-Required column with no accompanying brand.

records.verificationNote: Read pages 52-56 (printed pages 45-49) of the PDF, CARDIOVASCULAR AGENTS / ANTIHYPERTENSIVES section, position-parsed. Every ACE inhibitor found (lisinopril, enalapril, benazepril, ramipril, fosinopril, captopril, quinapril, moexipril, trandolapril, perindopril, plus their thiazide combinations) is Tier 1 with zero dots in any PA/Step/Dispensing/ACA/Limited-Distribution column - this is an unusually clean, unrestricted class on this formulary.

records.verificationNote: Read verbatim from the cardiovascular/'ACE Inhibitors' portion of the formulary (pdf pages ~30-31, printed pages 15-17): lisinopril, enalapril, benazepril, ramipril, fosinopril, quinapril, and captopril tablets/capsules are all listed at Tier 1 with no Requirements/Limits column entry, i.e. no PA/QL/ST. No brand-name ACE inhibitor (Prinivil, Zestril, Vasotec, Lotensin, Altace) is listed separately — all are fully generic.
